stories.headline: LAS crews speak out on sexual abuse on duty
stories.body: London Ambulance Service has launched the latest phase of its Respect campaign, with a paramedic describing being sexually assaulted on duty. LAS reported 462 sexual-abuse incidents in the year to July 2026.
stories.why: Almost two-thirds of women on ambulances in the NHS Staff Survey report unwanted sexual behaviour from the public.

stories.headline: Roadside blood test flags brain bleeds in minutes
stories.body: East Anglian Air Ambulance's BRAIN-FIRST programme uses a handheld analyser at scene. In its first 65 non-traumatic coma patients it caught every bleed, and it has since been used in more than 200 suspected serious brain-injury cases.
stories.why: Faster diagnosis at scene could help crews get patients to the right hospital first time.

stories.headline: EMAS prepares its first electric ambulances
stories.body: East Midlands Ambulance Service will gradually bring electric ambulances into frontline use from early 2027, under a nationally funded NHS programme. Crews will get specialist training first.
stories.why: The NHS aims for all new ambulances to be zero-emission from 2030, so this is the fleet of the future.

stories.headline: NEAS signs regional anti-racism pledge
stories.body: North East Ambulance Service has signed the Become the Bridge Anti-Racism Pledge, committing to practical action within 12 months to tackle racism in its workplace and in patient care.
stories.why: A fair, inclusive workplace matters for staff wellbeing and retention, and for the care patients receive.

stories.headline: College of Paramedics awards now open
stories.body: Nominations for the Royal College of Paramedics Honours and Awards are open until 12 February 2027. Student members can enter the Carol Furber Award with a reflective case study of up to 1,000 words.
stories.why: A chance to recognise great colleagues. The student winner is published in Paramedic INSIGHT.
